messages:
maya-support: heads-up — Acme reported TLS handshake failures to their private endpoint right after our scheduled egress IP rotation at ~02:14 UTC. They see 526 / tls handshake errors from their side.

maya-support: pasted the customer's curl output: `curl -v https://private-api.acme.internal --resolve 'private-api.acme.internal:443:REDACTED'` -> fails with `SSL: certificate subject name invalid` and `SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches`.

sophie-cs: pinging acme, they said they only allow specific source IPs for TLS-based routing on their edge (PaloAlto WAF) and do additional cert selection per source IP.

liam-engr: can you paste the full openssl s_client output from the failing run? need to see cert chain and SNI. Also which deployment ID?

maya-support: deployment id: redwood-private-42, customer org: Acme. s_client snippet from their engineer:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = AcmeCorp, CN = Acme Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=staging-gw.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Acme Edge CA
---
SSL handshake has read 1855 bytes and written 423 bytes
140736219843776:error:140940FC:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:ssl handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:\n
```
\nmaya-support: they also see server cert subject CN of 'staging-gw.acme.internal' (weird) — customer claims requests are routed to a staging cluster after our IP change.

derek-netops: looking at rotation logs — we rotated the ephemeral NAT pool for that VPC at 02:14:18 UTC as part of routine egress pool rebalancing. Affected egress range: 54.210.72.0/28 -> some machines got 54.210.72.13 replaced by 3.8.120.45 (example). I can confirm private-42 had an outbound nat from 54.210.72.13 -> 3.8.120.45 at 02:14.

derek-netops: deploy-bot shows rotation event: `rotate-egress: vpc=private-42 old=54.210.72.13 new=3.8.120.45 reason=pool-rebalance`

deploy-bot: rotate-egress event logged at 2026-06-07T02:14:18Z for redwood-private-42 (id redwood-private-42).

liam-engr: that matches the customer's symptom — their edge does source-IP -> backend mapping. When requests came from the new IP, their WAF routed traffic to a different backend cluster (staging) that presents a staging cert, hence the subject mismatch. This is not a certificate chain validation error from our TLS stack; it's a routing/categorization issue on their side.

maya-support: confirmed with Acme: they have an IP->pool mapping table that wasn't updated for the new IP and their HA group picked staging.

sophie-cs: next steps proposed to Acme: 1) add the new egress IP(s) (3.8.120.45) to their allowlist / source-ip mapping; 2) enable a short-term accept-all rule for our deployment while we coordinate; or 3) switch them to Reserved Egress so IPs are stable. They prefer not to do broad accept-all.

derek-netops: we can provision Reserved Egress for redwood-private-42. Ops checklist: file request -> allocate static egress -> coordinate cutover. ETA ~4 hours if approved.

liam-engr: temporary workaround for diagnostic repro: from a host in the private VPC run `curl -v --interface <internal-ip> https://private-api.acme.internal` or `curl ifconfig.me` to show current egress IP and paste into Acme ticket. Also get `openssl s_client -connect private-api.acme.internal:443 -servername private-api.acme.internal` to show the cert (to confirm it's staging cert).

maya-support: shared a compact repro message to Acme: "From our private instance we see outbound IP 3.8.120.45. Their edge returns staging cert CN=staging-gw.acme.internal. Please add 3.8.120.45 to your mapping or let us know if you want us to revert the rotation for this VPC while you update rules."

sophie-cs: I'll own the customer comms and get a formal approval for Reserved Egress. Also asked Acme to confirm which other IPs in the rotated block they need added.

derek-netops: one more note — rotation policy will avoid reassigning IPs from this VPC for 24h if we mark it as sensitive. We can flip that flag if Acme wants temporary stabilization without moving to Reserved.

maya-support: Acme responded: they will add the single new IP to their mapping, but asked if we can provide a list of possible future candidates to add proactively.

liam-engr: provided guidance link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/private-egress#ip-rotation (internal) and attached current pool snapshot: `54.210.72.0/28` -> active outings [54.210.72.9, 54.210.72.11, 3.8.120.45]. Mentioned rotations pick from shared pool and are subject to autoscaler.

sophie-cs: closing plan with Acme: 1) they add 3.8.120.45 now, 2) we mark private-42 as sensitive for 24h to avoid further churn, 3) we propose Reserved Egress as a durable fix and will send pricing.

maya-support: closing notes: root cause = egress IP rotation + customer-side IP->backend mapping that routes to staging cert. Action items: SOP to notify customers with strict IP->routing policies before egress rotations; add a pre-rotation webhook for private VPCs flagged as 'strict-egress-mapping'.

derek-netops: +1 to webhook. Filing follow-up ticket to infra backlog.

sophie-cs: Acme confirmed they updated mapping and TLS is green. Leaving thread open for 24h for any regressions. :white_check_mark:
